program.section_heading: Photography, Professional Certificate of Achievement and Associate in Arts
outcomes: Integrate conceptual elements with aesthetic and technical skills to create cohesive and memorable photographs.
Demonstrate full knowledge of the technical aspects of photography, including camera operations, exposure, lighting, and post-production, including software applications and printing.
Demonstrate an understanding of industry trends and professional practices related to a career in photography.
Conceive and produce a coherent portfolio of original work that meets department and professional industry standards.
Demonstrate an understanding of, and sensitivity towards, historical and contemporary issues of equity, race and representation in the photo industry.

notes: The section prints the Certificate of Achievement and the Associate in Arts together; the 27-unit major is the certificate's requirements. The A.A. adds general education and electives with no printed units, which are not recorded for this certificate.
The Program Outcomes list is printed once for the 'Certificate of Achievement/Associate Degree' and is shared by this award.
Catalog prints codes with leading zeros (PHOT 029, PHOT 031, PHOT 032, PHOT 035, PHOT 040, PHOT 045, PHOT 056); these were matched to closed-list PHOT 29, 31, 32, 35, 40, 45, 56.
List B is printed as 'PHOT158' without a space; recorded as PHOT 158.
List B's first line, 'Any course not used for List A 3', means unused List A courses (PHOT 152/153/154) may also count toward List B; not recorded as separate entries to avoid double listing.

PHOT 161 is printed with 3 units in List B, while the state file stores 1 unit; PHOT 162 is printed as 'Workshop: Portraiture Intensive' vs. state title 'Workshop: Portraiture and Studio Lighting'. Reviewer should check.
PHOT 030 'Beginning Film Photography', PHOT 030B, PHOT 033, PHOT 046 and PHOT 164 are not in the closed list and are marked catalog additions.
Careers are taken from the program description's named photographic fields, entry-level job areas and related fields.
